request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Discharge Summary:

Patient Information:
Name: Sarah
Age: 40
Gender: Female
Admission date: [Date]
Discharge date: [Date]
Reason for Admission: COVID-19 with symptoms of rhinorrhea, hyposmia, and ageusia

Hospital Course:
Sarah was admitted to the hospital with positive COVID-19 test results and mild symptoms of rhinorrhea, hyposmia, and ageusia. During her stay, she was treated with hydroxychloroquine and azithromycin, and her symptoms gradually improved. After three consecutive COVID-19 RT-PCR tests came back negative, she was discharged from the hospital in stable condition.

Follow-Up Care:
Sarah visited the Otolaryngology clinic one month after her discharge. She reported that her olfactory and gustatory functions had returned to normal. A nasal endoscopy revealed some watery discharge in the posterior nasal cavity without any sign of other lesions. Follow-up tests for olfactory and gustatory functions were conducted, which showed improvement in both her scores.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Summary:
Sarah, a 40-year-old female, was admitted to the hospital with positive COVID-19 test results and mild symptoms of rhinorrhea, hyposmia, and ageusia. After receiving treatment, she was discharged from the hospital in stable condition. During her follow-up visit, her olfactory and gustatory functions had returned to normal without any further treatment. A nasal endoscopy showed no sign of lesions. Her overall prognosis is good.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: U07**

COVID-19 is classified to category U07 (ICD-10-AM code U07.1, COVID-19 virus identified). The rhinorrhea, hyposmia, and ageusia are integral to the confirmed infection, so they are not coded separately. U is not among the chapter letters you listed, but U07 is the category the principal diagnosis belongs to.
